In mathematics, the '''oriented cobordism ring''' is a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] where elements are oriented [[cobordism class]]es<ref>Two compact oriented manifolds ''M'', ''N'' are [[oriented cobordant]] if there is a compact manifold with boundary such that the boundary is diffeomorphic to the disjoint union of ''M'' with the given orientation and ''N'' with the reversed orientation.</ref> of [[manifold]]s, the multiplication is given by the Cartesian product of manifolds and the addition is given as the disjoint union of manifolds. The ring is [[graded ring|graded]] by dimensions of manifolds and is denoted by
:<math>\Omega^{SO}_* = \oplus_0^\infty \Omega^{SO}_n</math>
where <math>\Omega^{SO}_n</math> consists of oriented cobordism classes of manifolds of dimension ''n''. One can also define an '''unoriented cobordism ring''', denoted by <math>\Omega^O_*</math>. If ''O'' is replaced ''U'', then one gets the [[complex cobordism ring]], oriented or unoriented.

In general, one writes <math>\Omega^B_*</math> for the cobordism ring of manifolds with structure ''B''.

A theorem of Thom<ref>{{cite web|title=MATH 465, Lecture 3: Thom's Theorem |url=http://math.northwestern.edu/~jnkf/classes/mflds/3thom.pdf}}</ref> says:
:<math>\Omega^O_n = \pi_{n}(MO)</math>
where ''MO'' is the [[Thom spectrum]].
